as_told.title: Gehlen Organization absorbed into the CIA

plain: After the Second World War, the story goes, America's wartime spy service, the OSS, took on Reinhard Gehlen, a German general who had run Nazi Germany's intelligence against the Soviet Union, and the story's title has him a Knight of Malta, a Catholic order, put in charge of West German intelligence. A guest named Dan Sheehan, repeating what he was told, describes Gehlen as "the head of the anti-Soviet and anti-Eastern bloc intelligence for the Third Reich." A researcher named Jason Jorjani tells it differently: the OSS "makes a deal with General Gehlen to absorb his entire Nazi spy network in Eastern Europe as part of the creation of the CIA," the US foreign intelligence agency. If true, Nazi spies would have been folded into the West's new intelligence services.
